title: Trusted-Model Weakness x Untrusted-Model Power: Compounding the Capability Gap in Control Protocols

original_idea.body: Run a control game where a small model monitors a larger one, sweep the size gap across model pairs, and plot how oversight reliability collapses as capability gap increases.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Maps where the weaker-overseer assumption of AI control breaks as capability gap grows.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Control game across model-size pairs, measure detection; uses ControlArena.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused detection-vs-gap curve; multiple model pairs add some effort.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Foundational scaling-limit question labs have weak incentive to attack; lab-independent, open models.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference across several model pairs; manageable on single GPU/API.

novelty.reasoning: Capability-gap framing discussed; the systematic detection-vs-gap sweep may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Trusted/untrusted framing studied; the gap-sweep curve may be open.
